grounding.title: Source check
grounding.only_unchecked: Not compared: the answer and its excerpts are in different languages

grounding.too_long: This answer is too long for the source check
grounding.disclaimer: The check compares the numbers, dates, times, codes, quotations and wording of each statement with the excerpts it cites and, in their language, whether it keeps their negations, puts names and values where they do and gives changes, comparisons and orders in time the same direction. A match does not prove a statement correct; a flag means: open the source and check.
grounding.reason_fact_elsewhere: {fact} is in {other}, not in the cited {label}.
grounding.reason_fact_context: {fact} is in {label}, but next to something else: “{found}”.
grounding.reason_name_missing: The name {fact} does not appear in {label}.
grounding.reason_uncited_found: No citation; the matching passage is {other}.
grounding.reason_uncited_missing: No citation, and {fact} is in none of the excerpts.
grounding.reason_low_overlap: Few of its words appear in {label}.
grounding.reason_unknown_citation: {found} is not one of the excerpts this answer was given.
grounding.reason_from_conversation: {fact} comes from the question or the conversation, not from an excerpt.
grounding.reason_not_delivered: {label} did not fit into the model's context.
grounding.reason_name_context: {label} names someone or something else here, not {fact}: “{found}”.
grounding.reason_relation_inverted: “{fact}” is the wrong way round: {label} says “{found}”.
grounding.relations: {n} {n:relation|relations} between values or events compared with the excerpts; {flagged} the wrong way round or not supported.
grounding.second_intro: Weak statements can get a second check: by an entailment model on this device, or by the AI judge, which sends each statement and its passages to your AI provider. It never turns a statement green; a contradiction keeps it amber.
grounding.second_intro_local: Weak statements can get a second check by an entailment model on this device; this answer stays on this device, so no AI judge is asked. It never turns a statement green; a contradiction keeps it amber.

grounding.second_result_entailed: Second opinion ({engine}): the excerpt supports it. Advisory only: the verdict stays.

receipt.title: Answer receipt
receipt.intro: A receipt lists the excerpts this answer cited, with a SHA-256 fingerprint of each file and the exact position of each passage. Anyone who has the same files can check that every excerpt is an exact, unchanged passage.
receipt.proves: Each workspace excerpt is an exact, unchanged passage of the file with the recorded fingerprint, at the recorded position, and belongs to this receipt through its Merkle proof. The source check can be recomputed from it.
receipt.not_proves: Who wrote the answer: a signature only shows the receipt is unchanged since a key signed it, and whose key that is only a public key from the signer shows. Nor which excerpts the model actually read, that the answer is correct, or anything about knowledge-base excerpts.
receipt.privacy: The file is created on this device and contains excerpts of your documents and fingerprints that identify them. It only leaves this device if you share it.
receipt.verify_intro: Choose a receipt and the original files. Both are read on this device; files are matched by their fingerprint, not by their name.
receipt.verify_pick_key: Signer's public key (optional, JWK or PEM)
receipt.verify_running: Checking the receipt against the files…
receipt.verify_invalid: This is not a valid Starpi receipt ({reason}).
receipt.verify_bad_key: The public key cannot be used ({reason}).
receipt.summary: {ok}/{total} workspace excerpts reproduced from your files
receipt.id_ok: The receipt hash matches its contents.
receipt.id_changed: The receipt was changed after it was created: its hash does not match its contents.
receipt.answer_ok: The answer text matches its fingerprint.
receipt.answer_changed: The answer text does not match its fingerprint.
receipt.format_v1: Receipt format v1: no Merkle tree and no signature.
receipt.merkle_ok: Merkle root reproduced from the citations; {valid}/{n} inclusion proofs valid.
receipt.merkle_failed: The Merkle tree does not match the citations: {valid}/{n} inclusion proofs valid.
receipt.check_file_missing: {label}: none of the chosen files has the recorded fingerprint.
receipt.check_passage_match: {label}: exact passage found in {file} at the recorded position.
receipt.check_passage_moved: {label}: the passage is in {file}, but not at the recorded position.
receipt.check_passage_mismatch: {label}: the text at the recorded position differs from the excerpt.
receipt.check_text_mismatch: {label}: the text extracted from the file differs from the recorded text.
receipt.check_text_version_differs: {label}: the file was read with a different extraction version; the extracted text differs.
receipt.check_chunk_mismatch: {label}: chunking the file today gives different chunk bounds.
receipt.check_chunk_version_differs: {label}: the chunking rules changed since the receipt was created.
receipt.check_proof_invalid: {label}: the inclusion proof does not lead to the Merkle root.
receipt.signature_unsigned_key: Not signed, although you chose a public key.
receipt.signature_trusted: Signed with the public key you chose ({alg}, key {key}) and unchanged since.
receipt.signature_embedded: Signed with the key in the receipt ({alg}, key {key}) and unchanged since. That does not show who holds the key: choose the signer's public key to check.
receipt.signature_invalid: The signature is invalid: the receipt was changed after it was signed, or the signature is forged.
receipt.signature_key_mismatch: Signed with key {key}, not with the public key you chose.
receipt.grounding_same: Source check recomputed for {n} statements: same verdicts as recorded.
receipt.grounding_differs: Source check recomputed for {n} statements: {diff} verdict(s) differ from the receipt.
receipt.grounding_conversation: Some verdicts used earlier chat turns, which receipts do not contain.

workspace.title: On-device workspace
workspace.description: Files are parsed, split into chunks and indexed with BM25 in a background worker on this device, and kept in this browser's storage unless you choose memory only. Nothing is uploaded or synced. Only when a model outside this device answers (the cloud assistant, NVIDIA NIM cloud through Starpi's server, or your own server) does file text go along with the question: in source mode the matching excerpts, in free chat the text of a file attached to that question (up to about 12,000 characters). Answers cite excerpts as [Doc: file, Chunk: n].
